findings.mechanism: startHeartbeat creates a setInterval whose callback closes over the session; the timer handle is stored only on session.heartbeat and is never clearInterval'd. Session.close()/Gateway.release() never clear it. The Node timer list keeps the interval (unref only stops it holding the event loop open, not from being referenced), so every closed session, with its socket, LoopbackSocket.written buffers, decoder, recent[] (up to 64 messages) and topics, stays reachable forever. The beat callback just returns when session.closed, but the interval keeps firing.
findings.cause: missing clearInterval(session.heartbeat) on close (src/session.js:303 close / src/gateway.js:72 release)
findings.evidence: After a connect/publish/disconnect wave via load.js runWorkload with 0 open sessions and forced GC: heapUsed 11.9MB at 2000 connections, 28.4MB at 4000, 60.9MB at 8000 (about 7KB retained per closed session, linear). Closed session's timer has _destroyed=false after clientHangUp.

findings.mechanism: Session.recent is a per-session array of recent messages.
findings.evidence: Code read: remember() shifts at RECENT_LIMIT=64, so bounded. Only retained long-term because the heartbeat timer pins the session (see first finding).
findings.discriminator: Capped at 64 entries per session; it is not independent growth.

findings.mechanism: Router.topics map of topic to Set of sessions.
findings.evidence: Session.close unsubscribes every topic and unsubscribe deletes empty topic sets; snapshot showed topics and sessions return to 0 after the workload.
findings.discriminator: Gateway.sessions and router.topics are emptied on close; sessions=0 after each wave.

findings.evidence: Keys are a fixed set of names plus closed_<reason> with a handful of reasons; latency array is fixed size.
findings.discriminator: Key cardinality is bounded, not per-session or per-user.
